yt_posts.topic: Dead coins: the ones everybody buried are the ones that pay
yt_posts.engagement_question: Could you hold a bag that looked completely dead for a full year, or would you have sold it like the Soros guy did?
yt_posts.body:
The coins everybody buried in August are the ones that pay in October.

I know how that sounds. Let me give you the receipts instead of the theory.

Tutorial. I called it during terror season, at the 2025 bear market lows. It ran 94x. Then it dumped through the October 10th crash and never recovered while everything else did. That is the moment a coin gets labeled dead. Every influencer moved on. The chart looked like a rug unless you zoomed out. I held it anyway, and three weeks ago it got short squeezed into another 130x.

That is not a one off. Velvet took 11 months to do 58x. LAB was called in October and did 350x in May. NYX did 550x in September, roughly a year after I called it. There is a coin called pumpkin that has been dead since Halloween, no content, no dev, nothing, and it just did a 6x over the month of August because people went looking for pumpkins again.

My favorite one is not even mine. A guy in a stream chat last September said he had bought a token called Soros two years earlier. It did nothing, so he sold it. Left alone in the wallet it would have been a 400x. He did everything right except the part where he did nothing.

So what is actually going on here?

A dead chart is not information about the project. It is information about attention. Attention leaves, liquidity goes with it, and the float falls asleep. Then one squeeze, one listing, one narrative, and the same coin reprices in a week because there is nobody left to sell it.

This is why I do not cut my dead bags. I take profits into the squeezes and rotate that money back out in 150 and 250 dollar slices, so the next 300x lands on a 400 dollar position instead of an 80 dollar one. My whole cost basis in LAB was 80 dollars and it came back as thousands. None of it went to a bank account.

Nothing here is financial advice, and most of these things do rug. The point is narrower: a flat chart is not a verdict, and dumping a dead bag for pennies is how people permanently exit the one position that was going to pay them.

So tell me straight: could you hold a bag that looked completely dead for a full year, or would you have sold it like the Soros guy did?

Hit like and subscribe if you would rather be early on the next one than hear about it after it runs.

yt_posts.topic: September breaks, October buys it all back
yt_posts.body_style: single stat opened wide, macro stacked behind it
yt_posts.engagement_question: Does Bitcoin reclaim that 50-week line before November, or do we lose 76K first?
yt_posts.body:
Bitcoin came 300 dollars short of the line that ends bear markets, and got thrown straight back under 76K.

300 dollars. That is the whole story of this week.

The 50-week SMA sits at 81,455. We tagged it minus a rounding error, got rejected, and by the next day we were printing 76 thousand handles with longs liquidated on the way down. We have been under that line since November of 2025, and it is not a moving average people draw for content: in completed bear markets, 11 of the last 13 reclaims of the 50-week on a weekly close meant the low was already in.

We just failed it by 300 dollars.

Now put the macro next to it. Chicago PMI came in at 47.1 against 57.9 expected, a swing of more than ten points off last month's 57.6. The Richmond Fed manufacturing print missed too. Housing keeps printing badly. And after Warsh spoke, the September Fed meeting is no longer a hold; it is a coin flip on a rate HIKE. We do not like hikes here.

So September gets its leg down. I think that is close to unavoidable, and I do not think it makes a new bottom, because a new bottom needs several bad things happening at the same time, not one bad PMI and a hawkish chair. Easy to say 70K. Easy to say 65K. Neither of those is a new cycle low.

Then October.

Here is what almost nobody gets right about October. It is not the bullish month. I pulled the stock market data for a presentation a few weeks back and October averages out to the middle of the pack, dead center of all twelve months. What it actually is, is the most volatile month of the year, which is the whole reason the famous crashes seem to live there. Not bearish. Swingy.

And swings are two directional.

My read is that it is going to be very hard to print a red October this year, whatever the news does. If things pump, sentiment buys it. If something breaks and we dump, everybody who missed the entire move off the lows finally gets their price. Either way the bid shows up, and red candles do not travel far when the whole market underneath them is waiting to get filled.

That is why I am not trying to time the exact bottom of September. I am trying to be positioned before October, not during it.

So where are you: does Bitcoin reclaim that 50-week line before November, or do we lose 76K first?

Hit like and subscribe if you want the macro read before it shows up on the chart.
